system:
You draft public warning messages for a national alerting authority.
You receive event inputs (each marked verified or unverified) and the issuing context.
Write one alert in English as CAP 1.2 fields.

- Use only facts present in the verified inputs. Do not add places, numbers, times or hazards that are not there.
- Leave unverified inputs out of the alert, and say why in `left_out`.
- `description` is the text shown on the phone by cell broadcast: plain words, under 280 characters, hazard + where + until when, if known.
- `instruction` is the protective action in one or two short sentences.
- Pick CAP values honestly: status from the context (Actual for a real event, Exercise for a drill), severity and urgency from the inputs.
- `note_for_reviewer` is one or two sentences for the human approver: what you were unsure about.
user:
Issuer: Demo national authority (stands in for the real issuer)
Context: EXERCISE / DRILL
Target area (chosen by the operator): Coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi (demo zone)

Event inputs:
1. [verified; NCM via WAM, 2026-02-16, https://www.wam.ae/en/article/byrq247-national-centre-meteorology-warns-dust-reduced] ABU DHABI, 16th February, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) warned today of active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds, raising dust and sand and reducing horizontal visibility to less than 3,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas. The Centre stated in a statement issued today that the weather conditions began at 10:30 and will continue until 18:00, urging the public to exercise caution, particularly when driving on external and open roads, due to the risk of sudden drops in visibility caused by blowing dust.
2. [verified; issuer profile] Issuer public site (demo): https://alerts.example.ae
3. [verified; institution reviewers] Objections from the institution reviewers to your previous draft. Fix what is within the verified inputs; do not add facts: Network operator and regulator reviewer objects (phone_text): Neither the English nor the Arabic phone text contains a recommended action for recipients. They only describe the hazard (winds raising dust and sand, visibility under 3,000 m) and its duration. The first page therefore cannot carry the action. This matters most in Arabic, where a UCS-2 page holds only about 41 characters (82 octets). Fix: Add a short protective action to both languages and put it at the very start, right after 'EXERCISE -' / 'تمرين -'. For example: 'Dust storm: drive with caution, reduce speed; people with breathing conditions stay indoors.' This puts the hazard and the action on page 1. Keep the location and time details after it. [cites Recommendation ITU-T X.1303bis: Common alerting protocol (CAP 1.2), p.22]

data.event: Blowing dust and sand, reduced visibility
data.headline: EXERCISE - Blowing dust and sand cutting visibility in coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi, until 18:00
data.description: EXERCISE - Blowing dust: drive with caution on external and open roads. Active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds cut visibility to under 3,000 m in some coastal and inland areas of Abu Dhabi, 10:30 to 18:00, 16 Feb 2026. Sudden visibility drops possible.
data.instruction: Take care, especially when driving on external and open roads, and be ready for sudden drops in visibility. Updates: https://alerts.example.ae
left_out: Reviewer's example action 'reduce speed' was not used as worded. NCM only urges caution when driving on external and open roads, so the action is limited to that.
Reviewer's example action 'people with breathing conditions stay indoors' was left out. No verified input mentions health advice.
Reviewer's example term 'Dust storm' was not used. NCM describes winds raising dust and sand, not a dust storm, so 'Blowing dust' is used instead.
Arabic phone text was not produced. This task asks for one English alert, so the Arabic version must be fixed separately with the same verified action wording.
data.note_for_reviewer: The protective action now opens the phone text right after 'EXERCISE -', as the reviewer asked, but it uses only NCM's verified advice (caution on external/open roads). Please confirm that tying NCM's 'some coastal and inland areas' to the operator-chosen Abu Dhabi demo zone is acceptable.
